kai: :rotating_light: noticing a sudden surge in KV paging on prod clusters serving the 'open-llama-awq' variant. p95/p99 token latency climbing and a bunch of backpressure in continuous-batching queues. metric snapshot attached below.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - kv_paging_rate > 5% across us-west-2-gpu-pool for model=open-llama-awq. PagerDuty: oncall-eng escalated.

ash (sara): can you paste the top logs/stack traces? is this correlated with any rolling deploy?

kai: pushed a quantization experiment this morning that enabled the awq kernel path for several models (auto-choose awq for int8). rollout started at ~08:12Z. here's the tail of the runtime warning and a small config diff: 

```
2026-03-15T08:13:02Z runtime WARN kv_cache: estimated_kv_size=2.4GB shard=3 model=open-llama-awq variant=awq
2026-03-15T08:13:04Z runtime ERROR paging: shard=3 spill_start, target_dir=/var/spill/gpu3
config change: "quant_kernel_selector": "auto" -> now choosing awq for int8
```

ash (ash): confirmed. on metrics: kv_memory_total per-host jumped ~2.1x after rollout. continuous_batch_queue_length spiked, which then caused batch building to hit our paging path. p99 latency for text-generation up ~4.2s.

maria: ops noticed some customer-facing 429s and a couple of 500s tied to staging -> prod traffic. Not widespread but noticeable on a few high-throughput customers (orgs A and C).

jules: quick mitigation options: 1) force fallback to the previous quant path (gptq/int8-fallback) by flipping kernel selector, 2) temporarily reduce continuous-batching max_tokens and max_batch_size, 3) enable strict eviction policy to drop cold prefixes. Which is fastest?

kai: fastest is toggling the kernel selector flag per-model to disallow awq. pushing that now as a hotfix flag: `runtime.features.quant_kernel_selector=prefer_gptq` -> will force the older int8 path. doing canary first on us-west-2-gpu-pool-2.

oncall-bot: HOTFIX DEPLOYED (canary) by kai at 2101234569. Monitoring...

ash: after canary the canary host's kv_memory dropped to normal and paging events stopped there. rolling the flag to the rest of the pool in 2m.

ops-bot: rolling update started: 6 hosts -> 6/6 updated.

maria: Customer A reported immediate improvement; their request error rate fell back to baseline. Marking customer-impacting = partial.

jules: follow-on config changes to avoid recurrence: - add per-variant kv_size_estimate in model manifest - safety throttle on kernel auto-selection when kv_mem > 1.2*baseline - alert on >1.5x kv_memory increase in 5m window

ash: live mitigation checklist (done):
- [x] Identify deploy that triggered change
- [x] Canary kernel selector rollback
- [x] Rollout flag to pool
- [x] Notify customers with known impact
- [ ] Postmortem + root cause analysis

kai: handing off to eng-sre for monitoring until next shift. @eng-sre please keep an eye on kv_paging_rate, continuous_batch_queue_length, and p99 generation latency for the next 4 hours.

eng-sre: acknowledged. we'll keep dashboards on and enable a temporary alarm to page SRE if kv_paging_rate > 3% again.

jules: immediate follow-ups (owners):
- model-team (jules): build kv footprint matrix for awq vs gptq vs int8-fallback across seq lengths 32/128/512. due EOD tomorrow.
- runtime (kai): add a runtime guard to cap kernel auto-upgrade when aggregate kv_mem > 1.5x baseline. due 72h.
- monitoring (ash): add synthetic that runs a short prefix-heavy prompt to detect kv blowups. due 48h.
- support (maria): reach out to impacted customers with summary and mitigation notes. done for A; schedule for C.

sara: quick note for the postmortem: include exact model revision and the kernel selection logic diff. we need reproducible test that shows why awq increased KV size (is it storing extra metadata or different dtype?).

kai: digging into model artifacts now. early suspicion: awq codepath stores denser KV caches due to block packing differences + different kv dtype alignment -> increases per-token kv footprint. also kernel picks slightly larger kv shard sizes.

oncall-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE - severity lowered to SEV-3 (partial customer impact mitigated).

maria: assigning follow-up ticket INF-3721 (kv-awq-footprint) for the model/runtime work.

ash: adding one more immediate safety: I'll open a short-term throttle rule to cap per-tenant QPS for high-throughput orgs if their requests cause the backend to exceed kv_mem threshold — will stage that as a soft throttle with telemetry only for now.

jules: thanks everyone. we'll schedule an incident review tomorrow morning. please paste any logs/screenshots into the ticket. closing live thread but keeping monitoring open. :white_check_mark:

eng-sre: logging all actions into the incident timeline and will attach dashboards.
